key_insight: Pre-fracture anemia was independently associated with a higher risk of nonunion after tibia and femur fractures, and risk increased with greater anemia burden.
clinical_relevance: Anemia status before fracture may help identify patients at elevated risk for impaired bone healing and nonunion.
method: Retrospective cohort study using commercial and Medicare claims data from 2016-2023
Adults 19+ with tibial or femoral fractures, continuous prior enrollment, and no baseline cancer
Compared pre-fracture anemia subtypes and burden against nonunion occurring 6-18 months after fracture
evidence_signal: In 326,673 adults, crude nonunion incidence was 42% higher with anemia, and adjusted hazard ratios remained elevated for tibia and femur fractures.
watch_item: Claims-based anemia and nonunion definitions may miss clinical detail, and some anemia subgroups had too few events for stable estimates.
paper_title: Pre-fracture Anemia Is Associated with Nonunion Following Tibia or Femur Fractures: A Retrospective Cohort Study
